articles.title: Scientists make stunning discovery that could help explain why life exists
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that the universe's fundamental physical constants may be finely balanced to make life possible. Even tiny changes to these constants could make liquids too thick or too thin for essential biological processes, potentially preventing life as we know it. Surprisingly, these life-friendly conditions existed billions of years before living cells appeared. The findings raise intriguing questions about why the laws of physics seem so well suited to life.
articles.content:
Imagine a universe where stars still shine, planets still form, and water exists, but liquids are so thick that living cells can barely function. Even with the chemical ingredients for life, the conditions might make living organisms impossible.

Scientists have uncovered a remarkable connection between the fundamental laws of physics and the ability of life to exist. Their findings suggest that even relatively small changes to some of the universe's most basic physical constants could dramatically alter how liquids flow, potentially preventing essential biological processes from taking place.

The discovery, detailed in a study published in Science Advances, came from physicist Kostya Trachenko at Queen Mary University of London. His theoretical analysis identified an additional constraint on the values of fundamental physical constants: They must permit liquids to move in ways that support life within and between cells.

The work raises a profound question about the universe. Why do the fundamental laws of nature have values that appear so well suited to the existence of life?

The Fundamental Constants That Shape Our Universe

Fundamental physical constants are numbers that govern how the universe operates. Examples include the mass and electric charge of an electron and the Planck constant, which plays a central role in quantum mechanics, the branch of physics that describes matter and energy at extremely small scales.

These quantities are generally considered universal and unchanging over time. Their values influence everything from the behavior of atoms and chemical bonds to the nuclear reactions that power stars and produce elements essential for life.

Despite their importance, scientists still do not know why these constants have the particular values we observe.

An important clue emerged in 2020, when Trachenko and his colleagues demonstrated that fundamental physical constants place a lower limit on the viscosity of liquids.

Viscosity describes how strongly a fluid resists flowing. Water has relatively low viscosity and pours easily, while honey and tar are much more viscous and move slowly. The researchers showed that there is a fundamental limit to how freely a fluid can flow, with that limit ultimately connected to the basic constants of nature.

The 2023 study took this connection much further by examining its implications for biology.

Why Tiny Changes to Physics Could Make Life Impossible

Every living cell depends on the movement of molecules. Nutrients must reach the places where they are needed, waste products must be transported away, and countless chemical reactions must occur in a liquid environment.

Another important process is diffusion, the natural spreading of particles through a fluid. Diffusion helps molecules move around cells and enables many of the chemical interactions required for life.

If the viscosity of those fluids changed too much, these processes could become severely disrupted. Liquids that were too thick might prevent vital materials from moving efficiently, while excessively low viscosity could also interfere with the controlled flow necessary for biological functions.

Trachenko explained the surprising connection:

"Understanding how water flows in a cup turns out to be closely related to the grand challenge to figure out fundamental constants. Life processes in and between living cells require motion and it is viscosity that sets the properties of this motion. If fundamental constants change, viscosity would change too impacting life as we know it. For example, if water was as viscous as tar life would not exist in its current form or not exist at all. This applies beyond water, so all life forms using the liquid state to function would be affected."

The implications extend beyond water. Although all known life depends on water, hypothetical organisms elsewhere in the universe might rely on different liquids. The same fundamental physical constraints would still influence how those liquids behave.

Trachenko suggested that the range of constants compatible with cellular life could be surprisingly narrow.

"Any change in fundamental constants including an increase or decrease would be equally bad news for flow and for liquid-based life. We expect the window to be quite narrow: for example, viscosity of our blood would become too thick or too thin for body functioning with only a few per cent change of some fundamental constants such as the Planck constant or electron charge."

These predictions come from theoretical models rather than experiments in which scientists actually changed fundamental constants. The precise limits that different forms of life could tolerate remain uncertain.

A Cosmic Mystery Billions of Years in the Making

What makes the findings especially intriguing is that the same fundamental constants that influence liquid flow also govern the nuclear reactions responsible for creating heavy elements inside stars.

Long before the first living cells appeared, stars were producing elements such as carbon and oxygen that would eventually become essential components of living organisms.

Physicists have long investigated whether the constants governing these nuclear processes must fall within certain ranges for complex matter to exist. But the ability to create life's chemical ingredients does not necessarily guarantee that life can function.

Trachenko's analysis showed that some physical properties governing liquid flow could change without disrupting the combinations of constants needed to produce heavy nuclei in stars.

In other words, a hypothetical universe might still produce the elements necessary for life while having liquids so viscous that cellular processes could not operate.

That means the conditions needed to support life may involve more than the ability to form stars, planets, and complex chemistry. The physical properties of liquids could impose additional requirements on the universe's fundamental constants.

Follow-Up Research Reveals a Surprising Connection to Blood

The investigation continued beyond the original discovery.

In a follow-up study published in January 2025 in The European Physical Journal E, Trachenko and colleagues examined how fundamental physical constants influence more complicated biological fluids, particularly blood.

Unlike water, blood is a complex mixture containing plasma, red blood cells, platelets, and other components. Its viscosity depends not only on molecular properties but also on how these components interact.

For example, red blood cells can form clusters that increase resistance to flow. As the blood moves faster, those clusters can break apart, allowing it to flow more easily. This behavior makes blood considerably more complicated than a simple liquid.

The researchers found something unexpected. Despite the enormous complexity of blood and the relatively large size of red blood cells, its viscosity remains surprisingly close, on a fundamental physical scale, to a theoretical value derived from basic physical constants.

They proposed that interactions between closely spaced blood cells may help explain this connection. Even though red blood cells are vastly larger than atoms, the forces acting where their surfaces approach one another involve distances small enough for molecular and quantum effects to matter.

The 2025 analysis also emphasized an important complication. Estimating which fundamental constants are compatible with life requires accounting for both the intrinsic properties of liquids, determined by fundamental physics, and the additional effects created by interactions among cells and molecules.

These findings offer a more detailed framework for investigating the connection between the universe's basic physical properties and the biological processes that depend on them.

Could the Laws of Physics Have Evolved?

The research also points toward an even deeper mystery: Why do the fundamental constants have values that allow so many different physical processes to work together?

One speculative possibility raised by Trachenko is that multiple forms of fine-tuning may be involved. The values that allow stars to manufacture heavy elements and those that permit liquids to support cellular life may represent separate requirements.

He suggested an intriguing analogy with biological evolution, in which different useful characteristics can emerge through separate processes.

Perhaps some broader evolutionary principle could help explain how nature arrives at combinations of physical properties capable of supporting stable structures and increasingly complex systems.

For now, this remains a conjecture. Scientists have not established that fundamental constants evolve through such a mechanism, nor have they determined why those constants possess their observed values.

Still, the connection between liquid flow and fundamental physics opens another way to investigate one of science's biggest unanswered questions.

Something as ordinary as water moving through a glass, or blood circulating through the body, may hold clues to why the universe has the physical properties that make life possible.
articles.reasoning: The article reports a significant scientific discovery revealing how fundamental physical constants are finely tuned to allow liquid flow essential for life, providing new insights into the conditions that make life possible in the universe. This breakthrough has broad implications for physics, biology, and our understanding of life's existence, making it inspiring and impactful for the general public.
articles.personality_title: Scientists find why liquid flow is key to life in the universe
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Scientists study fundamental physical constants, which are fixed numbers that control how the universe works. These constants affect everything from atoms to stars. Researchers want to understand why these numbers have the values they do.

**What happened** – Physicist Kostya Trachenko and his team found that small changes to these constants would change how liquids flow. Since living cells depend on liquids moving properly inside and between them, changes in liquid thickness (viscosity) could stop life from working. This discovery shows that the universe’s constants are finely balanced to allow liquids to flow just right for life.

**Impact** – This finding is important because it links the laws of physics directly to biology. It explains why life-friendly fluids like water have the right flow properties. Also, these conditions existed billions of years before life began, adding a new layer to why the universe supports life. The work even connects to blood flow, showing complex fluids follow the same physical rules.

**What's next step** – Scientists will study how different liquids and biological fluids behave under these physical limits. They will also explore if the values of fundamental constants could have changed over time or if they follow some natural selection process like evolution. This research could deepen our understanding of why the universe is the way it is.

**One-sentence takeaway** – A new discovery shows that the universe’s physical constants are precisely balanced to make liquids flow properly, which is essential for life to exist.
articles.personality_title_fr: Des scientifiques découvrent pourquoi le flux des liquides est essentiel à la vie dans l’univers
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Les scientifiques étudient les constantes physiques fondamentales, des nombres fixes qui régissent le fonctionnement de l’univers. Ces constantes influencent tout, des atomes aux étoiles. Les chercheurs cherchent à comprendre pourquoi ces nombres ont les valeurs qu’ils ont.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Le physicien Kostya Trachenko et son équipe ont découvert que de petits changements dans ces constantes modifient la façon dont les liquides s’écoulent. Comme les cellules vivantes dépendent du bon mouvement des liquides à l’intérieur et entre elles, un changement dans l’épaisseur (viscosité) des liquides pourrait empêcher la vie de fonctionner. Cette découverte montre que les constantes de l’univers sont finement réglées pour permettre aux liquides de s’écouler correctement pour la vie.

**Impact** – Cette découverte est importante car elle relie directement les lois de la physique à la biologie. Elle explique pourquoi les liquides adaptés à la vie, comme l’eau, ont les bonnes propriétés d’écoulement. Ces conditions existaient aussi des milliards d’années avant l’apparition de la vie, ajoutant une nouvelle dimension à la raison pour laquelle l’univers soutient la vie. Le travail se connecte même à la circulation du sang, montrant que les fluides complexes suivent les mêmes règles physiques.

**Prochaines étapes** – Les scientifiques étudieront comment différents liquides et fluides biologiques se comportent sous ces limites physiques. Ils exploreront aussi si les valeurs des constantes fondamentales ont pu changer avec le temps ou si elles suivent un processus de sélection naturelle comme l’évolution. Cette recherche pourrait approfondir notre compréhension de la nature de l’univers.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Une nouvelle découverte montre que les constantes physiques de l’univers sont précisément équilibrées pour permettre aux liquides de s’écouler correctement, ce qui est essentiel à l’existence de la vie.
articles.personality_title_es: Científicos descubren por qué el flujo de líquidos es clave para la vida en el universo
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Los científicos estudian las constantes físicas fundamentales, números fijos que controlan cómo funciona el universo. Estas constantes afectan desde los átomos hasta las estrellas. Los investigadores quieren saber por qué estos números tienen los valores que tienen.

**Qué pasó** – El físico Kostya Trachenko y su equipo encontraron que pequeños cambios en estas constantes cambiarían cómo fluyen los líquidos. Como las células vivas dependen del movimiento correcto de los líquidos dentro y entre ellas, cambios en el grosor (viscosidad) de los líquidos podrían impedir que la vida funcione. Este descubrimiento muestra que las constantes del universo están finamente ajustadas para permitir que los líquidos fluyan correctamente para la vida.

**Impacto** – Este hallazgo es importante porque conecta directamente las leyes de la física con la biología. Explica por qué líquidos amigables para la vida, como el agua, tienen las propiedades adecuadas para fluir. Estas condiciones existieron miles de millones de años antes de que comenzara la vida, añadiendo una nueva razón sobre por qué el universo sostiene la vida. El trabajo incluso se relaciona con el flujo de sangre, mostrando que líquidos complejos siguen las mismas reglas físicas.

**Próximo paso** – Los científicos estudiarán cómo diferentes líquidos y fluidos biológicos se comportan bajo estos límites físicos. También explorarán si los valores de las constantes fundamentales han cambiado con el tiempo o si siguen un proceso como la evolución. Esta investigación podría profundizar nuestro entendimiento de por qué el universo es como es.

**Conclusión en una frase** – Un nuevo descubrimiento muestra que las constantes físicas del universo están equilibradas con precisión para permitir que los líquidos fluyan correctamente, algo esencial para que exista la vida.

articles.title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president
articles.summary: Brad Smith calls for global rules on AI, and says the UK is in the "best position" to lead the charge.
articles.content:
Milk and washing machines are currently more regulated than AI, the president of Microsoft has said.

Brad Smith said there needed to be global safety rules in place, including a legal obligation to tell a "victim" if their system is breached by a rogue AI agent as well as deciding when outside evaluators should sign off on an AI product before it is released.

His comments put him at odds with President Donald Trump, who said the sector should regulate itself so US firms don't lose out to Chinese rivals.

But Smith said: "Right now, your washing machine is subject to more safety rules than AI. Every carton of milk that you see in the grocery store is subject to safety rules and inspection."

Demands for laws and rules to control AI have grown after experts in the sector said they believed the technology is a threat to humanity.

The bosses of the US-based AI giants such as Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind have all backed the idea of an AI development slowdown, but Trump has pushed against this.

Speaking to the BBC's Big Boss Interview podcast, Smith called AI both a "tool and a weapon" that urgently needed to be regulated.

"Let's get started today," he said.

He said firms need "emergency brakes" – often known in the industry as 'kill switches' – to pause or slowdown AI if it got out of control in some way.

He also said there should be a legal requirement for firms to write "incident reports" and tell victims if the technology goes rogue. He also suggested that independent government evaluators should vet new AI technology.

"We know how to do this for other products," Smith said. "We should build on that knowledge and think about how to apply it to AI."

Smith said the UK was best placed to drive forward these global rules for AI because of its AI Security Institute, external, launched during former prime minister Rishi Sunak's government as the AI Safety Institute.

"In the world of technology, in the tech sector, most people that I know would say, if you ask them, name the country that is the leader in having this technical capability, they would say, it's very simple. It's the United Kingdom. They are the best."
articles.reasoning: The article reports on a significant call from a major tech leader for global AI regulation, highlighting the urgent need for safety measures and legal frameworks to manage AI risks. This has broad societal implications given AI's growing impact and potential dangers. The focus on establishing global rules and safety protocols, including legal obligations and independent evaluations, represents a meaningful step toward responsible AI development with wide-reaching benefits.
articles.personality_title: Microsoft president urges global safety rules for AI
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Artificial intelligence (AI) is a fast-growing technology that can help people but also cause problems if not controlled. Right now, AI has fewer safety rules than everyday things like milk or washing machines.

**What happened** – Brad Smith, president of Microsoft, spoke about the need for global laws to make AI safer. He suggested that companies should have to tell people if AI systems cause harm and that independent experts should check AI products before they are used. He made these comments during a podcast interview, saying AI can be both a useful tool and a dangerous weapon.

**Impact** – Smith’s ideas are important because AI is becoming part of many parts of life, and without rules, it could cause serious problems. His call for “emergency brakes” or kill switches means AI could be stopped quickly if it acts badly. Also, having legal rules about reporting problems could help protect people from harm caused by AI.

**What's next step** – Smith believes the United Kingdom is in the best position to lead the world in creating these AI safety rules. This is because the UK has already started an AI Safety Institute to study and manage AI risks. If other countries follow, global rules for AI could soon become a reality.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Microsoft’s president calls for urgent global laws to make AI safer, with the UK leading efforts to protect people from AI risks.
articles.personality_title_fr: Le président de Microsoft appelle à des règles mondiales pour la sécurité de l’IA
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – L’intelligence artificielle (IA) est une technologie en pleine croissance qui peut aider les gens, mais aussi causer des problèmes si elle n’est pas contrôlée. Aujourd’hui, l’IA est moins réglementée que des produits quotidiens comme le lait ou les machines à laver.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Brad Smith, président de Microsoft, a parlé de la nécessité de lois mondiales pour rendre l’IA plus sûre. Il a suggéré que les entreprises doivent avertir les personnes si les systèmes d’IA causent des dommages et que des experts indépendants doivent vérifier les produits d’IA avant leur utilisation. Il a fait ces déclarations lors d’une interview, disant que l’IA peut être à la fois un outil utile et une arme dangereuse.

**Impact** – Les idées de Smith sont importantes car l’IA fait partie de nombreux aspects de la vie et sans règles, elle pourrait causer de gros problèmes. Son appel à des « freins d’urgence » ou « interrupteurs d’arrêt » signifie que l’IA pourrait être stoppée rapidement en cas de problème. De plus, des règles légales pour signaler les incidents pourraient protéger les personnes des dommages causés par l’IA.

**Prochaines étapes** – Smith pense que le Royaume-Uni est le mieux placé pour diriger le monde dans la création de ces règles de sécurité pour l’IA. Le Royaume-Uni a déjà lancé un Institut de sécurité de l’IA pour étudier et gérer les risques liés à l’IA. Si d’autres pays suivent, des règles mondiales pour l’IA pourraient bientôt devenir une réalité.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Le président de Microsoft appelle à des lois mondiales urgentes pour rendre l’IA plus sûre, avec le Royaume-Uni en tête des efforts pour protéger les gens des risques liés à l’IA.
articles.personality_title_es: El presidente de Microsoft pide reglas globales para la seguridad de la IA
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – La inteligencia artificial (IA) es una tecnología que crece rápidamente y puede ayudar a las personas, pero también causar problemas si no se controla. Actualmente, la IA tiene menos reglas de seguridad que productos cotidianos como la leche o las lavadoras.

**Qué pasó** – Brad Smith, presidente de Microsoft, habló sobre la necesidad de leyes globales para hacer la IA más segura. Sugirió que las empresas deben informar a las personas si los sistemas de IA causan daños y que expertos independientes deberían revisar los productos de IA antes de usarlos. Hizo estos comentarios durante una entrevista en un podcast, diciendo que la IA puede ser tanto una herramienta útil como un arma peligrosa.

**Impacto** – Las ideas de Smith son importantes porque la IA está presente en muchas partes de la vida, y sin reglas podría causar problemas graves. Su llamado a tener “frenos de emergencia” o interruptores para detener la IA significa que podría pararse rápido si se comporta mal. Además, tener reglas legales para reportar problemas podría proteger a las personas de daños causados por la IA.

**Próximos pasos** – Smith cree que el Reino Unido está en la mejor posición para liderar el mundo en crear estas reglas de seguridad para la IA. Esto se debe a que el Reino Unido ya creó un Instituto de Seguridad de IA para estudiar y manejar los riesgos. Si otros países siguen el ejemplo, pronto podrían existir reglas globales para la IA.

**Conclusión en una frase** – El presidente de Microsoft pide leyes globales urgentes para hacer la IA más segura, con el Reino Unido liderando los esfuerzos para proteger a las personas de los riesgos de la IA.
